 and healthy
 equipment 
 as safety helmet, safety shoes, 
 goggles, protective clothing, rubber gloves ... 
 etc
Don't smoke in the battery room.
Don't place any tools on top of battery cells (Danger of short circuit)
Never use the same tools on alkaline cells you may have used before on lead acid cells
All tools will be used must be insulated.
Never use a hydrometer used before on lead acid cells

Personal safety 
 and healthy equipment as safety boots, safety goggles, rubber gloves, rubber 
 apron ... etc

sections.text: Perform the monthly maintenance procedure from step 2 to step 9
In addition perform the following steps:

items: Perform the monthly maintenance procedure from step 2 to step 9

Measure and record the specific gravity of the electrolyte in each cell 
(The standard for above Varta cell type is 1,19 with a tolerance of + - 0,02).
Check and record the temperature of the electrolyte in each cell.
Disconnect AC supply to battery charger.

Read and record overall battery voltage immediately after AC power is switched off and then after fifteen (15) minutes for 
the duration of one hour. Continue recording the voltage every hour for eight (8) hours while observing at the same time that 
the voltage does not fall below 215 volts.
If voltage should fall below 215 volts, terminate test, place battery bank on float (high) charge for eight (8) hours.

When step 5 is completed, place selector switch to trickle (normal) charge and return battery bank to regular 
service.
Compare the readings you have taken to the readings recorded in previous years.

Batteries | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document outlines the 
 equipment inspection steps 
I3, which must be performed on an annually bases as indicated 
by Y1 in the title block.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued 
 and the 
 qualified maintenance staff carry the suitable safety 
 ID category,
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the 
 work area is required,
Use standard personal safety 
 and healthy
 equipment 
 as safety helmet, safety shoes, 
 goggles, protective clothing, rubber gloves ... 
 etc
Don't smoke in the battery room.
Don't place any tools on top of battery cells (Danger of short circuit)
Never use the same tools on alkaline cells you may have used before on lead acid cells
All tools will be used must be insulated.
Never use a hydrometer used before on lead acid cells
Personal safety 
 and healthy equipment as safety boots, safety goggles, rubber gloves, rubber 
 apron ... etc
Hydrometer, Tool
 set.
Perform the monthly maintenance procedure from step 2 to step 9
In addition perform the following steps:
Perform the monthly maintenance procedure from step 2 to step 9
Measure and record the specific gravity of the electrolyte in each cell 
(The standard for above Varta cell type is 1,19 with a tolerance of + - 0,02).
Check and record the temperature of the electrolyte in each cell.
Disconnect AC supply to battery charger.
Read and record overall battery voltage immediately after AC power is switched off and then after fifteen (15) minutes for 
the duration of one hour. Continue recording the voltage every hour for eight (8) hours while observing at the same time that 
the voltage does not fall below 215 volts.
If voltage should fall below 215 volts, terminate test, place battery bank on float (high) charge for eight (8) hours.
When step 5 is completed, place selector switch to trickle (normal) charge and return battery bank to regular 
service.
Compare the readings you have taken to the readings recorded in previous years.
